headline: Discussed planning for the 2026 Nature Based Climate Solutions grant cycle, including scoring rubrics and applicant orientation; no votes were recorded.
summary: Members discussed the 2026 Nature Based Climate Solutions grant cycle, including scoring rubrics for the grant and the new native plant pilot. They also discussed an orientation sheet for review committee members and community outreach about funded projects. The minutes record no votes or formal decisions.

Open Space Subcommittee Meeting Minutes 
 
 
November 2, 2026 at 4:30 PM 
 
311 North Avenue, Conference Room or Remote via Zoom 
 
 
Present: Scott Gustin, Dan Cahill, Zoe Richards, Rebecca Roman, Kelly Farrell, & Sharon Bushor.  
 
 
I. Discussion Items 
- Planning for 2026 Nature Based Climate Solutions grant cycle 
 
RR suggested an orientation sheet for the review committee before reviewing the 
applications.  In particular, explain that the individual scoring sheet is not final and can be 
adjusted following committee discussion.  RR asked about the review rubric.   
 
ZR said last year’s applicant pitch meeting opportunity was helpful.   
 
SG noted the NOFO for this year’s grant cycle.   
 
RR, archive / records of final reports would be helpful for reference.   
 
DC overviewed the NOFO.  The application period opens November 3 and closes December 
18.   
 
RR, the timeline needs to include a January BCB meeting for applicants to present to the 
Board.   
 
Review of scoring rubrics (NBCS and plant pilot).  The NBCS rubric is similar to last year’s.  
The native plant project is new for this year.   
 
RR had thought that stewardship zones were a priority for the native plant pilot, but they are 
not in the scoring matrix.  Dan, we want to cast a wide net for this initial pilot project.   
 
KF, it would be helpful to hear from applicants as to how the process/project went.  RR said 
it could be an opt-in rather than a requirement.  RR, maybe provide grantees with a feedback 
form for consideration of how to improve the process.
Discussion of orientation for review committee members.  RR requested a brief instructional 
sheet as to the process and consideration of the applications.   
 
Dan said he can have a draft orientation sheet ready to review at December meeting.   
 
II. Public Comment 
 
Sharon Bushor spoke in support of the scoring matrixes.  Do we ask applicants after-the-fact 
about their perception of the process?   
 
Dan said he’s been meeting with NPA’s and putting information out into the community as to 
resources, such as for stump grinding follow-up work for ash tree removal.  His group has 
only so much capacity.  We need help to improve outreach and community support.   
 
KF suggested maybe even something like a small sign in a pollinator garden that makes it 
known that it was created with support from the conservation legacy fund.   
 
RR, a note for next year, how will applicants inform the community about their project?  
How can we highlight the project’s successes?  Maybe have a conversation with Jules Shen?   
 
Dan, maybe in February or March we can talk about a comprehensive communications plan.  
RR, maybe we can talk in Open Space Subcommittee before a full board meeting (March mtg 
& April 2027 mtg, respectively). 
 
III. Adjournment 
 
5:25 PM.
